status_note: Items tagged verified_primary come from the RERA Act or K-RERA documents read on 2026-10-22. Items tagged general_knowledge are standard industry practice written without an official source and must be checked before they appear as fact in a script.

actors.does: Buys or controls land, gets approvals, registers the project with K-RERA, builds, markets and sells. Liable for the truth of its advertisements.

actors.who: Real estate agent / broker / channel partner
actors.does: Brings buyers for a commission. Must register with K-RERA before helping sell in a registered project.
Pays in stages and signs the agreement for sale. Can complain to K-RERA or the adjudicating officer.
Owns the land. In Karnataka only a promoter may register a project, so a landowner who wants to sell units must be or appoint a promoter.
K-RERA registers projects and agents, hears complaints and issues directions (s37). K-REAT hears appeals. Appeals from K-REAT go to the High Court.

buying_process_under_construction.detail: Search the RERA number on rera.karnataka.gov.in. See the declared completion date, status and quarterly updates.
Ask to see the sanctioned plan and commencement certificate. K-RERA registration requires plan approval and a commencement certificate first.
A lawyer should check title and land-use status. Not researched here; do not make claims.
A promoter cannot take more than 10% of the cost without a written, registered agreement for sale.
Karnataka has a model agreement (K-RERA 'sale agreement rules, 2020' listed on the site, not read).
70% of money received is kept in a separate account for the project's cost.
If possession is late, the promoter owes interest or a refund with interest on demand. Interest rate: SBI highest MCLR plus 2%.
Sale deed registration and transfer of khata. Specifics for Bengaluru were not verified.
K-RERA's own page says the promoter must rectify structural defects within two years of possession.

documents_buyers_ask_for.doc: RERA registration certificate and project page
documents_buyers_ask_for.proves: The project is registered and what the developer declared (dates, plans, promoter)
What may be built, including amenities
Built per plan and fit to occupy, at the end
Property tax record with the local body (rules not verified)
Ownership and no hidden charges (not researched)

what_realbrain_can_safely_explain: What RERA is and that a project's registration number can be searched on rera.karnataka.gov.in
That ads must carry the registration number and K-RERA website (s11(2))
That a developer cannot take more than 10% advance without a registered agreement for sale (s13)
That 70% of buyer money for a registered project goes into a separate account (s4(2)(l)(D))
That carpet area is the usable area inside the walls (s2(k))
What a completion certificate, occupancy certificate and sanctioned plan are
That a buyer misled by a false statement in an ad can claim compensation or a refund with interest (s12)
what_requires_verification_before_use: Anything about a specific project: registration, dates, approvals, amenities, price, khata
Anything about e-Khata, A/B-khata, GBA, B-to-A regularisation fees or deadlines
Land conversion, zoning and planning-authority approvals
Stamp duty, registration charges, GST and tax benefits
Rental yields, appreciation, loans and EMIs
The AI-label duty of an advertiser
known_uncertainties: Whether K-RERA applies the 2019 print placement rules to Instagram reels
Whether the 500 sq m and eight-apartment thresholds are 'either or' in every authority's practice, and whether Karnataka lowered them
Whether a newer K-RERA circular supersedes the 2019 advertisement circular
Direct labelling duty of advertisers under the IT Amendment Rules 2026 and whether the continuous-label draft became law
Whether a developer is a 'service provider' for CPA 2019 sections 21 and 89
